title: 💻 Asus Launches the 'Zephyrus G16'! Desktop Power in a Slim 1.64 cm Body... and a Cinematic Screen!
body: 💻 Asus Launches the 'Zephyrus G16'! Desktop Power in a Slim 1.64 cm Body... and a Cinematic Screen!

Asus has launched the new ROG Zephyrus G16 gaming laptop in Korea — a laptop with a 16-inch screen that combines the power of desktop computers with the slimness of ultra-light devices, an equation that was hard to achieve just a few years ago.

The device runs on the Intel Core Ultra 9 386H processor, which has 16 cores — four for performance, eight for efficiency and four for low-power efficiency — with speeds of up to 4.9 GHz, and an AI unit capable of 50 trillion operations per second, making it meet the requirements of Copilot+ PCs. The graphics card is from the GeForce RTX 50 series, up to the RTX 5070 at 115 watts, and the RTX 5070 Ti and above at up to 160 watts.

Despite this power, the device is only 1.64 cm thick and weighs about 1.85 kilograms, with a 2.5K OLED screen, a 240 Hz refresh rate and brightness of up to 1,100 nits — a cinematic screen by every measure — plus memory of up to 64 GB, fast storage of up to 2 TB and a 90 Wh battery.

In published tests, Cyberpunk 2077 exceeded 200 frames per second with DLSS 4 and 6x frame generation — a number that used to belong only to powerful desktop computers. The price is about 5.3 million Korean won, equivalent to about $3,900, in Korean stores.
Simply put: a gaming laptop with desktop power in a slim body no more than 1.64 cm thick, a cinematic screen and a high price... is it worth that price?
Would you prefer a powerful, slim laptop, or a cheaper, more powerful desktop computer?
